TYPE CHECK: The candidate value "wild-type" describes a genetic status/strain type rather than a disease state or diagnosis.
SOURCE CHECK: The value "wild-type" is present in the text (e.g., "wild-type M. agalactiae"), referring to the MS samples.
TRUTH CHECK: While "wild-type" is mentioned, it is not a disease state. However, the study is not a disease study; it compares two bacterial species. According to the field definition, "normal", "healthy", or "no disease" are safe defaults for subjects not part of a disease study. "Wild-type" is often used as a synonym for "normal" or "control" in genetic contexts, but the definition specifically lists "normal", "healthy", "no disease", and "disease free" as the safe defaults.
COMPLETENESS CHECK: The full set contains only "wild-type", which is a type mismatch for the "disease" field.
